ds: Illegal collection, export, treatment or dumping of hazardous or regulated waste, often disguised as second-hand goods or recyclables and shipped to countries with weak controls. Profits come from avoided disposal costs and falsified treatment records.

src.t: FATF, Money Laundering from Environmental Crime (2021)
Basel Convention on the Control of Transboundary Movements of Hazardous Wastes and their Disposal
UNEP and INTERPOL, The Rise of Environmental Crime: A Growing Threat to Natural Resources, Peace, Development and Security (2016)
Europol, public material on environmental crime and waste trafficking

rat: Waste firms, shippers and brokers disguising waste as used goods; cash to informal tippers and rotating shell operators.

ind.n: Waste shipped as used goods or recyclables
ind.cx: Containers described as used electronics, vehicles, plastics or metal scrap with signs of unsorted waste.
ind.fp: Second-hand trade is huge and legitimate.
ind.ds: Containers described as used electronics, vehicles, plastics or metal scrap with signs of unsorted waste.

ind.n: Collection firm paid low fees yet reporting large volumes
ind.cx: Waste firm bills clients far below market disposal rates.
ind.fp: Efficiency or subsidies may lower prices.
ind.ds: Waste firm bills clients far below market disposal rates.

ind.n: Licence or permit lacking or misused
ind.cx: Operator lacks the permit or uses another firm's permit for different waste.
ind.ds: Customer offering a regulated or permitted activity cannot evidence the required licence or registration, or operates under a licence held by another party.
ind.cn: Missing, misused or unverifiable licence or registration

ind.n: Shipments to countries with weak controls and few recycling facilities
ind.cx: Exports to destinations known as dumping sites.
ind.ds: Exports to destinations known as dumping sites.

ind.n: Cash payments to landowners or drivers for dumping
ind.cx: Payments to farmers, quarry owners or drivers for tipping.
ind.ds: Large or repeated cash payments to informal traders, producers or workers in extraction or supply chains.
ind.cn: Cash payments to informal suppliers or ground-level operators

ind.n: Short-lived waste companies with common directors
ind.cx: Companies appear, accumulate waste and vanish leaving liabilities.
ind.fp: Contractors may fail for commercial reasons.
ind.ds: Entities are repeatedly formed, abandoned or replaced by successors sharing directors, addresses or history of prior defaulted companies.
ind.cn: Short-lived or rotating entities with common controllers

ind.n: Mixed legal and illegal operations blending flows
ind.cx: Legitimate recycler also receives mislabelled loads and commingled revenue.
ind.ds: Legitimate recycler also receives mislabelled loads and commingled revenue.

ind.n: Adverse media or enforcement action over waste crime
ind.cx: Fines, seizures, or investigations tied to firm or owners.
ind.ds: Credible negative news, enforcement notices or investigations link the customer, its owners or associates to criminal, corrupt or regulated-sector misconduct.
ind.cn: Adverse media on customer or associates

ctl.ds: Maintains lists of higher-risk goods, species and commodity codes, tags relevant transactions and triggers extra documentary checks and screening of descriptions. It focuses scrutiny on the goods most associated with abuse.

ctl.n: Trade document review and consistency checking
ctl.ds: Trained staff and automated checks review goods, parties, routes, descriptions and codes across invoice, bill of lading and payment documents. It exposes mismatches and falsified paper.

ctl.n: Licence and permit verification for regulated goods
ctl.ds: Validates licences, permits, certificates and authorisations with the issuing authority and compares their scope with observed activity or shipments. It prevents genuine permits being misused or forged permits being accepted.

Compares declared unit prices, award values, fees and ancillary costs with reference databases, estimates and comparable contracts, and requires documented rationale for outliers. It detects over- and under-invoicing and inflated awards.

Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.

Maps suppliers and sub-suppliers back through the chain, down to plot, mine or farm level where relevant, and requires traceability of key inputs to origin. It makes hidden high-risk sources visible so they can be excluded or audited.

ctl.n: Counterparty capacity and trade profile assessment
ctl.ds: Tests whether a counterparty's size, history, equipment and sector make the traded volume and goods plausible, and models an expected trade profile to alert on deviation. It detects trading that is out of line with the business.

ctl.n: Country, corridor and port risk rating framework
ctl.ds: Maintains documented risk ratings of countries, corridors, ports and booking centres drawn from transparency, corruption and mutual-evaluation sources, updated on a schedule and after relevant events. The ratings feed due diligence, monitoring and limits.

ctl.n: Cash deposit profiling and peer benchmarking
ctl.ds: Compares cash deposits and withdrawals with expected activity, sector and location peers and declared turnover, alerting on outliers. It helps find cash that is inconsistent with the stated business.

Educates retailers, suppliers, hospitality providers and other partners to recognise and report suspicious patterns, and invites reporting channels. It extends detection to people who see activity before the institution does.

Runs continuous screening of customers, owners, introducers, suppliers and counterparties against curated news, leaks, regulatory notices and enforcement releases, with reliability grading and identity disambiguation. It surfaces negative information that registers and lists do not carry.

Links newly formed companies to failed or abandoned predecessors through shared officers, addresses, customers and bank details. It detects serial use of disposable entities to shed liabilities and move value.

Tests whether an entity has real operations such as premises, staff, stock and contracts through documents, site or virtual visits, open-source footprint and shell-risk indicators. It helps identify shell and front companies with no genuine activity.

Compares reported volumes with capacity, production, mass balance, concession size and national trade statistics to test whether quantities are physically possible. It exposes inflated, laundered or mislabelled flows.

Applies targeted enhanced checks to customer types or sectors known to be vulnerable to misuse, such as cash-intensive trades, money service businesses, high-value dealers, professional services, charities or waste handlers. Questions and evidence are tailored to how the sector normally operates.
